name: DR Congo
summary: Battling a large Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak: 6,757 confirmed cases and 3,267 deaths as of 7 September 2026, concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.

name: Uganda
summary: Has reported 20 cases linked to the Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak in neighbouring DR Congo.

name: Yemen
summary: Fighting has escalated around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as Houthi forces seize Red Sea islands and trade strikes with Saudi Arabia.

name: Saudi Arabia
summary: Targeted by Houthi missile and drone attacks on its southern air bases while conducting airstrikes in Yemen.

name: Ukraine
summary: Russia is holding State Duma voting in the occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, which Kyiv condemns.

name: Russia
summary: Holding State Duma elections on 18–20 September 2026, including in occupied parts of Ukraine.

name: United States
summary: Hosts the UN General Assembly's High-level Week and an upcoming Trump–Xi summit; the Federal Reserve raised rates to 3.75–4%.

name: China
summary: Preparing for a Trump–Xi summit in Washington as the October 2025 Busan trade truce nears expiry.

name: France
summary: Reporting 92 locally acquired West Nile virus cases across several regions as of 16 September 2026.

name: Liberia
summary: Reporting 33 Lassa fever cases, including 11 deaths, as of 30 August 2026.

name: Germany
summary: A malaria cluster in Frankfurt has reached 8 infections and 3 deaths.

name: Italy
summary: Reporting 12 Usutu virus cases as of 9 September 2026.

name: Kosovo
summary: Former president Hashim Thaçi was sentenced to 25 years for war crimes by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague.

name: New Zealand
summary: Parliament passed the India free trade agreement 93–29, cutting tariffs on about 95% of exports to India once in force.

name: India
summary: Imports 88.7% of its crude oil, so the Red Sea crisis feeds into its fuel bill and the rupee. Its free trade agreement with New Zealand, signed on 27 April 2026, cleared New Zealand’s Parliament.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Europe's second-largest economy and a global financial centre, and a permanent UN Security Council member that left the EU in 2020.

name: Japan
summary: The world's fourth-largest economy and a major exporter of cars and electronics; it imports almost all of its oil and gas.

name: South Korea
summary: A leading maker of memory chips, ships and cars, still technically at war with North Korea under the 1953 armistice.

name: Brazil
summary: Latin America's largest economy and a top exporter of soybeans, iron ore, coffee and beef; home to most of the Amazon rainforest.

name: Canada
summary: A top crude oil exporter that sends most of it to the United States, its largest trading partner.

name: Australia
summary: The world's largest iron ore exporter and a major supplier of coal and LNG, with China as its biggest customer.

name: Mexico
summary: The United States' largest trading partner and a manufacturing hub for cars and electronics under the USMCA trade deal.

name: Indonesia
summary: The world's largest archipelago nation and its biggest producer of nickel and palm oil.

name: Türkiye
summary: A NATO member that controls the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits linking the Black Sea to the Mediterranean.

name: Argentina
summary: A major exporter of soybean meal, beef and lithium, with a long history of high inflation and debt crises.

name: South Africa
summary: Africa's most industrialised economy and the world's leading producer of platinum and chromium.

name: Pakistan
summary: The world's fifth-most-populous country, a nuclear-armed neighbour of India, and heavily reliant on IMF support.

name: Bangladesh
summary: The world's second-largest garment exporter after China, and highly exposed to floods and cyclones.

name: Iran
summary: Holds some of the world's largest oil and gas reserves and borders the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil passes.

name: Israel
summary: A high-tech economy whose conflicts with Hamas in Gaza, Hezbollah in Lebanon and Iran shape regional security.

name: Egypt
summary: Operates the Suez Canal, a key East-West shipping route whose earnings fell sharply when Red Sea attacks diverted ships.

name: Nigeria
summary: Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers.

name: Ethiopia
summary: Africa's second-most-populous country, seat of the African Union, and builder of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile.

name: Kenya
summary: East Africa's largest economy and a regional hub for trade, finance and tech, with the port of Mombasa.

name: Sudan
summary: A civil war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces since April 2023 has caused the world's largest displacement crisis.

name: Iraq
summary: One of OPEC's largest oil producers; oil provides most of the government's revenue.

name: Syria
summary: Rebuilding after more than a decade of civil war; Bashar al-Assad's government fell in December 2024.

name: Afghanistan
summary: Ruled by the Taliban since August 2021 and facing one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises.

name: United Arab Emirates
summary: A Gulf hub for trade, aviation and finance; Dubai's Jebel Ali is the Middle East's busiest port.

name: Qatar
summary: One of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas, all shipped through the Strait of Hormuz.

name: Vietnam
summary: A fast-growing manufacturing hub for electronics and clothing, used by many firms moving production out of China.

name: Thailand
summary: Southeast Asia's car-making hub and a major rice exporter, with tourism a large part of its economy.

name: Philippines
summary: An archipelago in disputes with China over parts of the South China Sea; money sent home by overseas workers supports its economy.

name: Taiwan
summary: Makes most of the world's most advanced chips; China claims the island, making the Taiwan Strait a key flashpoint.

name: North Korea
summary: A nuclear-armed state under heavy UN sanctions that regularly tests ballistic missiles.

name: Myanmar
summary: In civil war since the February 2021 military coup, with armed groups holding large parts of the country.

name: Venezuela
summary: Holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, but years of economic collapse have driven millions to emigrate.

name: Colombia
summary: A major exporter of oil, coal and coffee, still working to end decades of armed conflict.

name: Spain
summary: The eurozone's fourth-largest economy and one of the world's most visited countries.

name: Poland
summary: One of the EU's fastest-growing economies and the main transit route for Western aid to neighbouring Ukraine.

name: Lebanon
summary: Still recovering from a financial collapse that began in 2019 and from the 2024 war between Israel and Hezbollah.

name: Chile
summary: The world's largest copper producer and second-largest lithium producer.
